If a CGSSB (formerly Vyapam) profile has not already been created, complete new Profile Registration first, uploading a recent photograph with a light-coloured background (JPG/JPEG format, 50 KB to 100 KB) and a scanned signature (JPG/JPEG format, 50 KB to 100 KB).

important_instructions: Caste, date of birth, local residence, and educational qualification certificates are not to be attached with the online application; all certificates will be verified later by the appointing authority, and the candidate is solely responsible for the accuracy of information submitted. A valid email ID is mandatory for every applicant. The admit card will be uploaded on the CGSSB website approximately 7 days before the exam and must be downloaded from the candidate's profile; it will not be sent by post. Candidates must reach the exam centre at least 2 hours before the exam for identity verification and frisking; the main gate closes 30 minutes before the exam start time (i.e., 9:30 AM for a 10:00 AM exam), after which no entry is permitted. Candidates must carry the admit card, a black or blue ballpoint pen, and an original photo ID (Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN Card, or Aadhaar Card). Only light-coloured, half-sleeved clothing is permitted; black, dark blue, dark green, purple, maroon, and dark chocolate-coloured clothing is not allowed. Only slippers are permitted as footwear, and no ear jewellery is allowed. Candidates cannot leave the exam hall during the first and last 30 minutes of the exam. Communication devices, electronic devices, watches, purses, pouches, scarves, belts, and caps are strictly prohibited inside the exam hall. There is no negative marking in the written exam. Candidates may raise objections to the provisional answer key online, with a fee of ₹50 per question; objections without supporting proof will not be considered, and the expert committee's decision on the final answer key is final. There is no provision for re-checking or re-evaluation, as OMR sheets are evaluated by machine. For help with the online application, candidates may contact 0771-2972780 (10:00 AM–5:30 PM on working days) or the mobile helpline 8269801982 (10:00 AM–5:30 PM, including holidays).

content_sections.heading: CGSSB NSSK26 Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for these posts follows a multi-stage process combining a physical efficiency test, a written exam, and (for driver posts) a trade test. Application scrutiny: Only candidates meeting all eligibility conditions are permitted to the physical efficiency test stage. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - completed: Conducted by the department for the 7 non-Station-Officer posts, out of 100 marks; General category candidates required a minimum of 50 marks, SC/ST/OBC candidates a minimum of 40 marks. Events included 100m Race, Long Jump, Shot Put, and Pull-ups/Beam-bar (25 marks each). Candidates who qualified were forwarded to CGSSB for the written exam stage. Written Exam (NSSK26) - current stage: 100 objective-type questions of 1 mark each, General Knowledge and Logical/Analytical Reasoning, 2-hour duration, no negative marking. Qualifying marks: General category - 40, SC/ST/OBC - 30. Trade Test (Driver / Driver-cum-Operator only): An additional 100-mark trade test; General category minimum 50 marks, SC/ST/OBC minimum 40 marks. Bonus marks: Up to 5 marks each (maximum 10 marks total, even with more than two qualifications) for: (a) a Heavy Motor Vehicle driving licence - not applicable for Driver/Driver-cum-Operator posts themselves, (b) national-level sports proficiency as a winner in a competition organised directly under the relevant national sports federation, and (c) an NCC 'C' certificate. Final Merit List: Prepared based on the total of PET marks + Written Exam marks + Bonus marks (bonus calculated separately), category-wise, following reservation rules.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for CGSSB NSSK26 Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Only candidates who already qualified in the department's physical efficiency test can apply for the NSSK26 written exam. The application must be submitted online through the CGSSB portal. Visit the official CGSSB website - vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in or cgssb.cgstate.gov.in. If a CGSSB (formerly Vyapam) profile has not already been created, complete new Profile Registration first, uploading a recent photograph with a light-coloured background (JPG/JPEG format, 50 KB to 100 KB) and a scanned signature (JPG/JPEG format, 50 KB to 100 KB). Log in to the profile and open the "NSSK26" written exam application link. Fill in the required application details and submit the form online. Pay the applicable examination fee online as per category. Download and keep a printout of the successfully submitted application form for future reference.

faq.question: Q1. What is CGSSB NSSK26 Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is the written recruitment examination conducted by the Chhattisgarh Karmachari Chayan Mandal (CGSSB) for the posts of Store Keeper, Vahan Chalak (Driver), Vahan Chalak-cum-Operator, Mechanic, and Watch Room Operator under the Chhattisgarh Fire & Emergency Services and SDRF department.

faq.question: Q2. Which posts are covered under the CGSSB NSSK26 written exam?
faq.answer: Only 5 posts: Store Keeper, Vahan Chalak, Vahan Chalak-cum-Operator, Mechanic, and Watch Room Operator. Station Officer, Fireman, and Wireless Operator (Contract) from the same original advertisement are not part of this written exam.

faq.question: Q3. How many vacancies are there under NSSK26?
faq.answer: 153 vacancies across the 5 covered posts, out of the 295 total posts in the original 12.06.2025 advertisement.

faq.question: Q4. What is the last date to apply online for CGSSB NSSK26?
faq.answer: 7 September 2026 (Monday), up to 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q5. What is the educational qualification required?
faq.answer: It varies by post - mainly Class 12 (10+2) pass, with additional requirements such as an HMV driving licence for Driver posts and an ITI Diesel Mechanic diploma for the Mechanic post. See the Eligibility section above for post-wise details.

faq.question: Q6. What is the age limit for CGSSB NSSK26?
faq.answer: 18 to 28 years as on 1 January 2025, with a general relaxation of 5 years and further category-based relaxations as specified in the notification.

faq.question: Q7. What is the application fee for CGSSB NSSK26?
faq.answer: ₹350 for General category, ₹250 for OBC, and ₹200 for SC/ST/PwD candidates for the written exam stage.

faq.question: Q8. How can I apply online for CGSSB NSSK26?
faq.answer: Through the CGSSB website (vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in or cgssb.cgstate.gov.in), after completing profile registration if not already done, followed by filling and submitting the written exam application form.

faq.question: Q9. What is the selection process for these posts?
faq.answer: Physical Efficiency Test (already completed), followed by a written exam, a trade test for Driver posts, and bonus marks for specific qualifications, with final merit based on the combined score.

faq.question: Q10. What is the salary/pay level for these posts?
faq.answer: Pay Matrix Level 4 for Store Keeper, Vahan Chalak, Vahan Chalak-cum-Operator, Mechanic, and Watch Room Operator. Exact in-hand salary figures are not specified in the notification.
